Article Title: Indian consulate in UAE issues warning over biometric fraud targeting nationals
Article Text:
The advisory urged nationals not to share their passports, Emirates IDs, biometric data, including eye, face or fingerprint scans, or personal and financial credentials with unauthorised individuals or agencies under any circumstances.

NEW DELHI: The consulate general of India in Dubai has warned Indian nationals in the UAE, particularly blue-collar workers, against handing over biometric data. The warning advised the workers against unauthorised agents claiming to help with visa regularisation, Emergency Certificates, Exit Permits, Emirates IDs or employment, after reports of fraud involving the misuse of fingerprints and facial scans.In an advisory issued on Monday, the consulate said it had received information about individuals and agents allegedly exploiting Indians seeking assistance with immigration and documentation procedures. The fraudsters reportedly ask victims to provide fingerprints or face scans, which can then be used without their knowledge to conduct financial transactions, open bank accounts or obtain loans and credit cards in their names.The consulate cautioned that such misuse could leave victims liable for financial obligations or transactions they did not authorise. In some cases, those affected could also face multiple fines, travel bans and even imprisonment.The advisory urged nationals not to share their passports, Emirates IDs, biometric data, including eye, face or fingerprint scans, or personal and financial credentials with unauthorised individuals or agencies under any circumstances.It also clarified that biometric information required for procedures such as exit permits, Emirates IDs or visa regularisation must be provided only at official UAE Government facilities or counters. People were specifically warned against submitting such information through private individuals, agents or third-party service providers claiming to be authorised by UAE authorities.The consulate also sought to dispel a potential source of confusion by stating that biometric information is not required for certain consular services.The advisory said the Consulate General of India in Dubai and the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi "DO NOT require any fingerprint scan or face/eye scan from applicants for the issuance of a passport or emergency certificate."It warned that any person or agent demanding such information while claiming to represent the Indian Embassy or consulate would be engaging in fraudulent activity and should not be entertained.Indians approached by unauthorised individuals seeking biometric data or Emirates IDs have been advised to contact the Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra through the toll-free number 80046342, WhatsApp or SMS at 00971543090571, or email pbsk.dubai@mea.gov.in to verify credentials or seek assistance.The consulate urged Indian nationals living in or visiting the UAE to exercise caution, independently verify the credentials of anyone offering immigration or documentation-related services, and report suspicious activity to the Indian consulate and the relevant UAE authorities.
Article Summary: The warning advised the workers against unauthorised agents claiming to help with visa regularisation, Emergency Certificates, Exit Permits, Emirates IDs or employment. The fraudsters reportedly ask victims to provide fingerprints or face scans, which can then be used without their knowledge to conduct financial transactions.

Article Title: Flyers asked to give handwriting samples after threat note causes Air India Express international flight to divert
Article Text:
Representative image (PTI photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian security establishment have finally decided to take the menace of hoax bomb threats that cause expensive diversions head on. An Air India Express Dammam-Delhi nonstop was forced to divert to Ahmedabad after a tissue paper with the words “bomb red 430” written on it and a box, both in black ink, drawn on it was found in the lav. After landing in Ahmedabad and following the required protocol, the security authorities additionally decided to conduct a handwriting test on all the 32 passengers and see if the expensive prank was played by one of them.“They asked the airline to give the same tissue paper and then organised the same colour pen. Six tissues were sought for each passenger. Now let us see if they find a match,” said sources. It is not yet known if this test managed to nab the person who allegedly wrote this threat note.The standard protocol for such situations is taking the aircraft to a remote parking bay; checking all passengers and cabin and check-in baggage thoroughly before clearing it to take off again. All this was followed on Monday too at Ahmedabad. The handwriting test was conducted on top of that.An Air India Express spokesperson said: “One of our flights from Dammam to Delhi was diverted to Ahmedabad as a precaution and in keeping with security protocols after being notified of a specific bomb threat.The government-appointed bomb threat assessment committee (BTAC) was alerted immediately, and all security procedures promptly initiated. The flight landed and all guests have been disembarked safely. The aircraft will be released for operations after necessary security checks are completed.”Indian carriers have suffered huge losses due to hoax threats in recent years. While tracking a call making such a claim is difficult due to advancement in technology, tackling on board threatening notes if written by someone onboard the affected flight could help tackle this menace. Monday’s handwriting test decision, say sources, was taken by BCAS and CISF. “Why the same has not been done in the past beats us,” said a senior pilot.Airlines and airports in India had received 999 hoax bomb threats between Jan 1 and Nov 14, 2024 — more than 10 times the number in 2023. The threats to both domestic and international flights were made mostly through social media and had disrupted air travel in India.
Article Summary: Airlines and airports in India had received 999 hoax bomb threats between Jan 1 and Nov 14, 2024 — more than 10 times the number in 2023. The threats to both domestic and international flights were made mostly through social media and had disrupted air travel in India.

Article Title: SC asks Centre, states why retail acid sale cannot be completely banned to curb attacks
Article Text:
The SC bench asked the Centre and states to respond within four weeks on a policy decision to either ban the retail sale of acid or impose strict restrictions on it. (Photo: PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday asked the Centre and the states why retail sale of acid should not be banned after an acid attack survivor complained that the SC-prompted 2013 guidelines of the Union government remain on paper even as girls continue to suffer physical disfigurement and lifelong mental trauma from acid attacks.Continuing with its strong stance against those jilted lovers accused of throwing acid on girls leading to severe physical disfigurement, loss of eyesight and lifelong mental trauma, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the Centre and states to respond within four weeks on a policy decision to either ban retail sale of acid or impose strict restrictions on it.This direction came after acid attack survivor Shaheen Malik, who runs an NGO to help girls who suffered trauma and scars of acid attacks, told the bench that every day three girls face a similar fate and there should be a complete ban on the retail sale of acid. She cited a case of three girls, two from Okhla in Delhi and one in Haryana, who were blinded by acid attacks. “How many more girls must suffer,” she asked while pushing for a complete ban.Accepting that acid should be supplied for the purpose of research and educational institutions, the bench said banning across-the-counter sale is the first option. In the alternative, it proposed whether retail sale of acid can be restricted only to those who are above 50 years of age after they give in writing the purpose behind such purchases.The data should be collated on a dashboard for ready reference of law-enforcing agencies on acid available in private hands.Senior advocate Saurabh Kirpal told the bench that strict guidelines framed by the SC in the Laxmi case in 2013 said acid continues to be available across the counter. The bench said the 2013 guidelines must have become obsolete now and asked additional solicitor general Archana Pathak Dave to submit fresh guidelines from the Centre on this issue.The bench also sought a status report on implementation of its May 9 directions to the states and Centre seeking schemes for rehabilitation of acid attack survivors, which could include preferential government employment and, in the absence of which, a monthly honorarium, lifelong free medical treatment and free education. SC also said it is desirable to include in the school curriculum the preventive measures, post-attack treatment and emergency protocol.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court asked the Centre and states to respond within four weeks on a policy decision to either ban retail sale of acid or impose strict restrictions on it. The direction came after acid attack survivor Shaheen Malik, who runs an NGO to help girls who suffered trauma and scars of acid attacks, told the bench that every day three girls face a similar fate.

Article Title: Kenney, Sikh leader share dais as Bhagwat makes global Hindu call
Article Text:
Bhagwat’s visit came despite demands from New Democratic Party and civil-society groups that he be denied entry to Canada. The venue was disclosed shortly before the programme amid security concerns.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A day after telling a New York audience that a Hindu who wanted Muslims excluded from India could not remain a Hindu, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat Monday used his first visit to Canada to cast Hindus as builders of an “exemplary society” worldwide and India as a “vishwaguru” serving humanity, not a “mahashakti” seeking dominance.The speeches shared themes of oneness, but differed in emphasis. In New York, amid protests and criticism of RSS, Bhagwat addressed concerns about exclusion; in Toronto, he explained how Hindu society should organise and lead internationally without imposing its beliefs.“The word Hindu cannot be defined by any specific language, through any specific worship or through any living style,” he said. The dais reflected that wider outreach: former Alberta premier and federal cabinet minister Jason Kenney and Kashmir Singh Dhaliwal of the Khalsa Diwan Society joined Bhagwat, placing a senior Canadian political figure and a representative of a Sikh institution alongside the RSS chief at a gathering opposed by sections of the South Asian community.“We have to build our society in every country, all over the world, which is an exemplary society for the world,” Bhagwat said at the “Hindu Vishwa Bandhu — Embrace the World in Friendship” event. The programme in Vaughan, in the Greater Toronto Area, was organised by Canadian Hindus for Outreach, Relations and Dialogue.Presenting India’s global role as one based on service rather than power, Bhagwat said: “It became ‘vishwaguru’, not ‘mahashakti’.”Whenever help had been sought during an international crisis, he said, India had not refused. “This is the tradition. This is the DNA of Bharat.”Bhagwat said the RSS organised Hindus “exactly for this purpose — and nothing else”, describing the purpose as developing individuals who would dedicate themselves to serving humanity.The RSS chief coupled the call for organisation with a message on civic responsibility. People connected with India but settled elsewhere, he said, “have to be honest, contributing citizens of that country”. At the same time, they should take to the world an outlook in which individuals, society and the environment could progress without harming one another.He said this should be done through conduct rather than imposition. “We don’t force,” Bhagwat said. “We are the leaders who lead from within and lead by example.” He added: “Hindus respect all. Hindus accept all.”Going beyond the familiar expression “unity in diversity”, Bhagwat said Hindu tradition also recognised “diversities of unity”. Different identities, he argued, were expressions of an underlying oneness. “Diversity is never a problem for unity,” he said. “All the diversities are expressions of unity.”Bhagwat’s visit came despite demands from New Democratic Party and civil-society groups that he be denied entry to Canada. The venue was disclosed shortly before the programme amid security concerns.
Article Summary: Bhagwat’s visit came despite demands from New Democratic Party and civil-society groups that he be denied entry to Canada. The venue was disclosed shortly before the programme amid security concerns. Bhagwat said the RSS organised Hindus “exactly for this purpose — and nothing else”

Article Title: CM Vijay releases Mettur Dam water for delta irrigation
Article Text:
(Photo: AM Shudhagar) The Mettur dam is traditionally opened on June 12 every year to facilitate the cultivation of kuruvai in the Cauvery Delta region. The opening was delayed this year as water levels in the Cauvery basin reservoir remained low.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

METTUR (SALEM): Chief minister of Tamil Nadu C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday released water from the Mettur Dam to meet the drinking water requirements and support samba cultivation in the Cauvery delta districts, the rice granaries of the state.As of Tuesday morning, the dam’s water level stood at 91.56 feet, with a storage of 54.452 tmc ft and an inflow of 10,857 cusecs. Water Resources Department officials said the release will be continuously monitored and regulated according to irrigation needs.Departments including Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Water Resources, and Revenue and Disaster Management have been directed to coordinate with district administrations to ensure effective utilisation. The government stressed that every cubic foot of water must benefit farmers, warning against illegal pumping, unauthorised extraction, and violations of permitted irrigation schemes.Joint monitoring teams comprising officials from the Electricity Distribution Corporation, Water Resources Department, Revenue Department, and Police will patrol day and night to prevent misuse.Reaffirming Tamil Nadu’s legal entitlement to Cauvery water, the chief minister said the state would not compromise on its rights upheld by the Cauvery Arbitration Final Award and the Supreme Court’s 2018 verdict.The government continues to pursue legal and administrative measures to secure the state’s share.Acknowledging the deficit in the southwest monsoon and the impact of El Niño, Vijay said the release was a planned measure to manage limited resources and safeguard samba cultivation. Farmers were urged to adopt medium-duration rice varieties and water-saving methods such as direct seeding.“Let us use water sparingly, ensure it reaches the end user, and make samba cultivation a success,” the chief minister appealed.
Article Summary: The Mettur dam is traditionally opened on June 12 every year to facilitate the cultivation of kuruvai. The opening was delayed this year as water levels in the Cauvery basin reservoir remained low. As of Tuesday morning, the dam’s water level stood at 91.56 feet.

Article Title: Translating the Reliance ethos into a blueprint for nation-building
Article Text:
Translating familial empathy into enterprise resilience

Democratising technology for a billion aspirations

Reclaiming soft power and passing the baton

There is a prevailing wisdom in global business schools that suggests the larger an enterprise grows, the colder it must become. Scale, the theory goes, demands a clinical detachment. Yet, in the heart of India's corporate landscape, a remarkably different experiment has been playing out for decades. Here, the traditional Indian family ethos has not been discarded as an archaic social structure but rather leveraged as a sophisticated business strategy.The recently released Reliance documentary, 'Parvah Hai Toh Parivar Hai', pulls back the curtain on this machinery. It offers a case study of what happens when the ethics of a household extend to a conglomerate employing hundreds of thousands, and ultimately to a nation of 1.4 billion people.Stripping away the complex financial jargon often associated with India's largest enterprise, the film reveals a foundational philosophy rooted in care, trust, and self-reliance. It asks a compelling question: can familial empathy actually drive a nation's socio-economic trajectory?At the corporate level, this paternalistic model is far more than a warm metaphor. It operates as a highly effective structural framework. The fundamental premise that care defines a family dictates how the company handles its human capital. During moments of intense crisis, such as health emergencies or natural disasters, this responsibility translates into the swift mobilisation of healthcare, isolation facilities, and emergency resources.This culture of protective support builds a rare institutional resilience, fostering a fiercely loyal ecosystem. Recalling the early days of setting up Jio Studios, an executive describes the deep personal involvement of the leadership. "I remember Mukesh Bhai and Manoj Bhai laying out their vision for the media business," she notes. "I remember thinking, do I have to pay to work here because this kind of mentorship is something that money cannot buy. "When creative and professional ventures face unexpected headwinds, this cushion of corporate confidence remains largely intact. Actor Ranveer Singh, reflecting on his collaborations with the conglomerate, highlighted this unusual patience. "I was given all the love, all the support and all the encouragement even at a time when my movies were not doing well," he shares in the film. "Career ups and downs. But to have received that kind of support meant a lot to me. It's nothing short of a blessing, an honour and a privilege to be associated with the Ambani family."However, the true test of any family-led business model lies in its ability to step outside its own perimeter and serve the wider community. For Reliance, modern nation building has meant translating massive corporate capacity into accessible public utility. Having already rewired India's digital landscape by making high-speed data universal through Jio, the enterprise is now looking towards the next frontier.The leadership frequently questions how their scale affects the masses. According to the documentary, the next step involves using new age technologies to bridge socio-economic gaps. "How does it affect the 1.4 billion people of India as we democratise information," the film asks, noting that generative artificial intelligence is "now democratising intelligence amongst 1.4 billion people."The ambition is to create tools that serve every stratum of society. The narrative paints a stark rural reality, envisioning a person in Bhagalpur "able to really use an AI tutor to teach himself or a farmer who is able to really understand what his food productivity would be." As the leadership points out, with this knowledge, "he is able to think more, he is able to do more, he is able to earn more and that is I think the ultimate goal for us. "Recognising that there are many Indias cutting across different income classes, the company is pivoting toward voice-first interfaces designed for the country's vast linguistic diversity. The documentary rightly points out that "Indians actually converse with technology by voice first rather than text." It is framed as a massive opportunity "which truly only an Indian company can solve." This ethos of mass accessibility comes directly from the top. As Mukesh Ambani directed his team regarding their massive streaming footprint: "The business is always important but I want consumers to experience our innovation."Beyond digital infrastructure, nation building requires fierce cultural stewardship. This household-led framework views corporate success as a catalyst for preserving national identity. Noting that foreign companies have historically dominated the sector, the documentary asserts, "There was no reason why an Indian company should not be leading the charts on media."Through Jio Studios, the mandate is bold: "What we want to do is claim back the narrative of India, especially young India." By backing massive commercial cinema alongside globally recognised projects, the conglomerate is actively shaping India's cultural footprint. Furthermore, spaces like the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre serve a dual purpose. "The vision of Mrs. Ambani and the vision of our centre is bringing the best of the world to India and the best of India to the world," the film notes.As the company approaches its 50th year, it stands at a critical juncture. Mukesh Ambani frames this generational shift not as a standard corporate handover, but as a continuation of core values. "Akash, Isha and Anant are only representatives of the young leaders," he explains. "And they will take our values. They will build an India of our dreams."At its heart, the enterprise remains anchored by its dining table roots. "To me, family is everything. I feel privileged that four generations of our family live together," shares Nita Ambani. This restless drive is perhaps best captured by 88-year-old V. Balasubramanian, who has spent 62 years at Reliance. He shares, "When I go away from this world, Dhirubhai is waiting there. We will start another Reliance Industries there and start working there and building up another empire. "Ultimately, the Reliance narrative suggests that India's economic rise is deeply intertwined with business models that align commercial scale with societal care. By treating a nation as an extended family, the company offers a compelling, distinctly Indian blueprint for modern nation building.
Article Summary: Reliance documentary, 'Parvah Hai Toh Parivar Hai', pulls back the curtain on this machinery. It offers a case study of what happens when the ethics of a household extend to a conglomerate employing hundreds of thousands, and ultimately to a nation of 1.4 billion people.

NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs on Monday categorically rejected a ruling by World Bank-constituted Court of Arbitration on Indus Water Treaty, terming it an "illegally constituted" organisation.In a statement, MEA said that New Delhi's decision to put the water treaty with Pakistan in abeyance "will remain in force.""This so-called Court was constituted by the World Bank in patent breach of the terms of the Treaty and India categorically rejects its so-called award, just as it has firmly rejected all prior pronouncements by this illegally constituted body," the ministry said."India has never recognised the existence in law of this illegally-constituted and so-called Court of Arbitration, and has consistently maintained that the very establishment of this alleged arbitral body constitutes a grave violation of the Indus Waters Treaty . Accordingly, India has never appeared before this body and has refused to take any cognisance of its earlier pronouncements," it added.Also read: 'India could use water as weapon': Pakistan minister as Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance The ministry also said that the Court of Arbitration has no "jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India’s sovereign decisions.""Its pronouncements, now or in the future, will have no effect on India’s actions in connection with the projects being undertaken by India," MEA said.This comes hours after the Court of Arbitration said that the grounds on which India decided to put the Indus Water Treaty in abeyance did not “justify suspension or termination.”“Accordingly, the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force, and India must observe its obligations under the Treaty,” the court saidNew Delhi put the agreement in abeyance following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year.Since then, Pakistani leaders have repeatedly called water their “red line” and threatened India over the move, describing it as an “act of war.”
Article Summary: Ministry of external affairs on Monday categorically rejected a ruling by World Bank-constituted Court of Arbitration on Indus Water Treaty. Ministry said that New Delhi's decision to put the water treaty with Pakistan in abeyance "will remain in force" Ministry also said that Court has no "jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India's sovereign decisions"

Article Title: IMD predicts below-normal rainfall over country in September
Article Text:
India to witness above avg temperature in September; rainfall likely to be below normal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Monthly rainfall over the country as a whole is most likely to be below normal in Sept, the last month of the monsoon season, said IMD Monday - an indication that the four-month rainy season is likely to end with overall deficient cumulative rainfall, as was predicted earlier due to the impact of El Nino.IMD said Aug, which reported a deficit of more than 16% in monthly rainfall in the country despite good rains in certain parts, was the warmest Aug in India since 1901, recording a mean temperature of 28.010°C.Region-wise, South peninsular India recorded its second-warmest Aug since 1901. East and northeast India recorded their third-warmest, while northwest India saw its fifth-warmest, Aug in 126 years.So far, the country as a whole has reported a deficit of 14% in cumulative (June 1-Aug 31) rainfall, despite ‘normal’ rainfall in July. In June, the deficit was as high as 35%. Out of a total of 741 districts assessed for monsoon rainfall distribution, 312 (42%) received ‘below-normal’ rainfall and 38 districts (5%) reported large deficient rainfall till Aug 31.A forecast of ‘below-normal’ rainfall in Sept may lead to a deficit in overall kharif acreage. Though the sowing of most seasonal crops is almost complete, with a decline in acreage of nearly 2% compared with the corresponding period last year, low rainfall in Sept implies an increase in input cost due to farmers’ spending on irrigation of standing crops.“Spatially, many parts of the country are likely to receive below-normal rainfall, but some areas of northwest, northeast, east, east-central and south-east peninsular India are likely to receive ‘normal to above-normal’ rainfall,” said IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.He said “strong El Niño conditions” are currently prevailing over the equatorial Pacific Ocean, with sea surface temperature remaining above normal across central and eastern equatorial Pacific. “These conditions are expected to strengthen further in the coming months,” said Mohapatra, hinting at its negative impact on Sept rainfall.El Niño is invariably associated with a weak monsoon and a harsh summer in India.At present, neutral Indian Ocean Dipole conditions prevail over Indian Ocean, which are likely to persist through Sept.This means that monsoon may not benefit from this climatic phenomenon as only positive IOD helps increase rainfall activities.
Article Summary: IMD said Aug, which reported a deficit of more than 16% in monthly rainfall in the country despite good rains in certain parts, was the warmest Aug in India since 1901. In June, the deficit was as high as 35%. Out of a total of 741 districts assessed for monsoon rainfall distribution, 312 received ‘below- normal’ rainfall.

Article Title: Not the era of war to end of war: PM Modi reiterates peace message to Putin
Article Text:
"Time to move away from endless war to end of war": PM Modi tells Russian Prez Putin on sidelines of SCO summit

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With still no end in sight to the Russia-Ukraine war, PM Narendra Modi renewed his message of peace to Russian President Vladimir Putin saying on this occasion that it was time to move from an endless war to the end of war for the sake of humanity.Modi delivered the message in his opening remarks before a bilateral meeting with Putin on the margins of the SCO heads of state summit in Bishkek in which the leaders focused on expanding cooperation in energy, defence, innovation, space, fertilisers and people-to-people linkages.The endless war to end of war message is the latest in a series of televised statements by Modi before Putin for the return of peace, beginning with his assertion in 2022 - frequently cited by the Western world and even making it to the G20 Bali Declaration that year - that this wasn't the era of war. That message too was delivered on the margins of another SCO summit in Samarkand. He followed it up with a message to Putin in Moscow in 2024 - in the midst of an outrage in the West over his Russia visit - that no solution can be found on the battlefield.Modi told Putin in Bishkek that India supports all efforts for peace and will continue to do so in the future, adding that an early end to the war was the call of humanity and also the message from the land of Buddha and Gandhi.“Every day spent in the war pushes humanity back. And every step taken towards peace fills humanity with new hope and enthusiasm. We will have to move from an endless war to an end of war, which is very important for humanity's well-being,” said the PM.“That all issues are resolved peacefully as soon as possible is the call of humanity. This is the message of India. This is the message of the land of Gandhi and the land of Buddha - the path to peace,” said Modi, adding that he was looking forward to welcoming Putin for the BRICS summit. India's balancing act on the war saw Modi travelling to Ukraine a few months after his visit to Russia in 2024.According to foreign secretary Vikram Misri, Modi conveyed to Putin India's readiness to do whatever is feasible and necessary at India's end to move the conflict towards an end because "it is exacting a very heavy toll on the global community at large"."Had extensive discussions with President Putin. Discussed the full range of the India-Russia Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership. It is gladdening to see significant progress across various sectors in recent years," said Modi in a post on X.In his own televised statement, Putin acknowledged Modi's personal attention to the development of bilateral ties. Putin also said Russia was preparing "seriously" for the BRICS summit in India and highlighted that over the past 10 years, the number of Indian students in Russia has shot up to 40,000.According to an Indian readout, the leaders exchanged views on India-Russia engagement in the multilateral arena, in particular in BRICS under India’s Chairship for 2026. “They also shared perspectives on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, including the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region which have impacted maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers,” said the Indian readout, adding that Modi reiterated dialogue and diplomacy was the way forward in resolving conflicts.The two leaders agreed to remain in touch to further strengthen the partnership, acknowledging its growth and resilience against the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainties.
Article Summary: Modi delivered the message in his opening remarks before a bilateral meeting with Putin on the margins of the SCO heads of state summit in Bishkek. The leaders focused on expanding cooperation in energy, defence, innovation, space, fertilisers and people-to-people linkages. Putin acknowledged Modi's personal attention to the development of bilateral ties.

Article Title: Government terms arbitration award on Indus Waters Treaty ‘illegal’
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Govt slammed an award by the “illegally constituted so-called Court of Arbitration (CoA)” concerning interim measures and status of the Indus Waters Treaty , recalling India’s position that the court has no jurisdiction to pronounce on India’s sovereign decisions. India had responded similarly to another award issued by the court in May this year.On this occasion though, according to a Reuters report from Amsterdam, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague said that India must uphold the Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan and must also limit work on an hydroelectric plant it is building in J&K.Govt maintains that this court was created in violation of the 1960 IWT which in any case has been put in abeyance by India because of Pakistan’s support to cross-border terrorism.“Today, the illegally constituted so-called Court of Arbitration has issued what it termed as an award concerning Interim Measures and Status of the Indus Waters Treaty. This so-called court was constituted by World Bank in patent breach of terms of the Treaty and India categorically rejects its so-called award, just as it has firmly rejected all prior pronouncements by this illegally constituted body,” MEA said.The ministry said that India has never recognised the existence in law of this illegally-constituted and so-called Court of Arbitration, and has consistently maintained that the very establishment of this alleged arbitral body constitutes a grave violation of the Indus Waters Treaty.“Accordingly, India has never appeared before this body and has refused to take any cognisance of its earlier pronouncements,” it said, adding that the court’s awards, now or in the future, will have no effect on India’s actions in connection with the projects being undertaken by India. The MEA also reiterated India’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance remains in force.The Permanent Court of Arbitration said the Indus Water Treaty remained fully in force, as India had no justification for ending or suspending the agreement.“India must observe its obligations under the Treaty, including those relating to the design and operation of its hydro-electric projects on the Western Rivers,” the intergovernmental court said.
Article Summary: India slams an award by the “illegally constituted so-called Court of Arbitration (CoA)” concerning interim measures and status of the Indus Waters Treaty. Govt maintains that this court was created in violation of the 1960 IWT.

Article Title: SC: Externment orders cannot be passed routinely, require reasons
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Holding that forcing a person to stay out of a city or district affects freedom guaranteed by the Constitution, SC on Monday ruled that a govt cannot pass an externment order routinely and must pass a reasoned order to justify such harsh measures.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed an externment order passed by Raigarh district magistrate directing a person to remove himself from the district and contiguous districts for one year. The order was passed against him as multiple criminal cases were pending and the district authority apprehended that his presence would create further problems in the area and nearby districts.“An order of externment directly impinges upon valuable fundamental freedoms guaranteed to a citizen and, therefore, cannot be made as a matter of routine. Further, merely because multiple criminal cases have been filed against a person would not, ipso facto, be a ground for ordering externment,” the bench said.Before exercising such power, the DM is required to arrive at a bona fide and informed subjective satisfaction that circumstances warrant such an extreme measure and externment is necessary, it said.The bench said the authority is not expected to render a judgement as a court of law but the order must nonetheless disclose, at least in broad terms, the reasons for such satisfaction.“The existence of objective material and a discernible nexus between such material and the conclusion reached are indispensable safeguards against arbitrary exercise of power,” it said.Quashing the order under Chhattisgarh Rajya Suraksha Adhiniyam, SC said the externment order fell short of statutory requirement. “The order does not indicate the material on the basis of which such conclusion was reached. No reasons are forthcoming to demonstrate why the third respondent (Raipur DM) considered the situation grave enough to necessitate the appellant’s externment,” it said.
Article Summary: SC quashes Raigarh DM order, says multiple criminal cases alone not grounds for such action. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed an externment order. The order was passed against him as multiple criminal Cases were pending and the district authority apprehended that his presence would create further problems.

Article Title: HC reinstates bank official sacked without inquiry over hashtag campaign
Article Text:

SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir high court has set aside the dismissal of a J&K Bank executive sacked without an inquiry into an alleged #TortureKashmir hashtag campaign on social media, ruling that a financial institution’s managing director “cannot be trusted with the drastic power to dismiss an employee without investigation”.“The President and governor are high constitutional functionaries and, therefore, they can dispense with the services of an employee without holding an inquiry in appropriate cases. But the same level of trust cannot be reposed in an officer of the level of managing director and CEO of a bank,” the single-judge bench of Justice Sanjay Dhar said in its verdict last Saturday.The petitioner, Saadut Hussain Pampori, joined J&K Bank as a computer engineer in June 1995 and rose to deputy general manager by 2022, serving as an officer on special duty to the chief minister from 2016 to 2018 under the BJP-PDP govt led by Mehbooba Mufti.The bank’s then MD suspended him on April 15, 2024, pending investigation into misconduct before ordering his dismissal on July 15 that year under Clause 12.29 of the officers’ service manual.The dismissal followed a report by DGP (CID) based on “credible sources, as also from discreet enquiries”. The report accused Pampori of spreading misinformation about alleged state-backed atrocities on Kashmiris.The court held that information gathered from sources or through discreet enquiries by DGP does not qualify as an “investigation” under Clause 12.29, since the process involves no collection of evidence or recording of witness statements.Justice Dhar drew a line between Clause 12.29 and Article 311(2)(c), under which govt may terminate an employee without the normal procedure if satisfied that retention is prejudicial to state security.J&K administration has dismissed nearly 100 govt employees under that provision.Clause 12.29, the court said, lays down specific preconditions, including an investigation by a state, Union territory or central agency, before an employee can be sacked.Quashing the order against Pampori as “not sustainable in law”, the court restored him to the post he held before his dismissal, albeit allowing the bank to proceed against him afresh.
Article Summary: J&K HC has set aside the dismissal of a bank executive sacked without an inquiry into an alleged #TortureKashmir hashtag campaign on social media. Saadut Hussain Pampori joined J&K Bank as a computer engineer in June 1995 and rose to deputy general manager by 2022.

Article Title: IMD predicts ‘below normal’ Sept rainfall, Aug was the warmest Aug in India since 1901
Article Text:
India is bracing for below-average rainfall this September, signaling an early end to the monsoon season with overall inadequate precipitation.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Monthly rainfall over the country as a whole is most likely to be ‘below normal’ in Sept, the last month of the monsoon season, said IMD on Monday — an indication that the four-month rainy season is likely to end with overall deficient cumulative (June-Sept) rainfall as predicted earlier with high probability due to the impact of El Nino.The Met department said August, which reported a deficit of more than 16 percent in monthly rainfall in the country despite good rains in certain parts, was the warmest August in India since 1901, recording a mean temperature of 28.01 degrees Celsius.Region-wise, August in south Peninsular India was the second-warmest August since 1901, whereas it was the third warmest for east and northeast India, and fifth warmest for northwest India in the past 126 years.So far, the country as a whole reported a deficit of 14 percent in cumulative (June 1-Aug 31) rainfall, despite ‘normal’ rainfall in July. In June, the deficit was as high as 35 percent. Out of a total of 741 districts assessed for monsoon rainfall distribution, 312 districts (42 percent) received ‘below normal’ rainfall and 38 districts (5 percent) reported large deficient rainfall till Aug 31.A forecast of ‘below normal’ rainfall in Sept may lead to a deficit in overall kharif crop acreage.Though sowing of most of the seasonal crops is almost complete with a decline in acreage by nearly 2 percent compared to the corresponding period last year, low rainfall in Sept means an increase in the input cost due to farmers’ spending on irrigation of standing crops.“Spatially, many parts of the country are likely to receive below-normal rainfall, but some areas of northwest, northeast, east, east-central and south-east Peninsular India are likely to receive ‘normal to above-normal’ rainfall,” said IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.He said currently “strong El Niño conditions” are prevailing over the equatorial Pacific Ocean, with sea surface temperature (SST) remaining above normal across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. “These conditions are expected to strengthen further in the coming months,” said Mohapatra, hinting at its negative impact on Sept rainfall.El Niño, characterised by the warming of ocean surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is invariably associated with a weak monsoon and a harsh summer in India.At present, neutral Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) conditions prevail over the Indian Ocean and the forecasts from the Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecast System (MMCFS) indicate that neutral IOD conditions are likely to persist through Sept. It means the monsoon may not benefit from this climatic phenomenon as only positive IOD helps increase rainfall activities.IMD noted that the extreme weather events (lightning, thunderstorm and heavy rains) took 113 human lives in Aug. Mohapatra, however, said this figure can be cross-checked with the data compiled by the states.
Article Summary: India is bracing for below-average rainfall this September, signaling an early end to the monsoon season with overall inadequate precipitation. August, which reported a deficit of more than 16 percent in monthly rainfall in the country, was the warmest August in India since 1901.

The Congress on Monday hit out at the government over India's 7.8 per cent GDP growth in the April-June quarter, saying the figure was "not an economic spring" and presented a "Greatly Distorted Picture" of the state of the economy.The opposition party questioned why the country's economic growth was not translating into jobs and prosperity, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the first-quarter performance as an "exemplary" and "herculean feat".Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the quarterly GDP numbers did not reflect what he described as depressed private investment sentiment, both domestic and foreign."The quarterly GDP numbers, such as they are reported, present a GDP - Greatly Distorted Picture - of the economy. They do not convey the decidedly depressed private investment sentiment in the economy - both domestic and foreign," Ramesh said in a post on X.He also claimed that consumer confidence was sluggish, household savings rates had fallen and debt had reached record highs."Consumer confidence is very sluggish, hitting its lowest point since COVID and on a relentless downward trajectory since November 2025. Prices of household essentials are galloping.Educated unemployment is at alarming levels. The unabated trade deficit with China is wreaking havoc," Ramesh said.He further claimed that the concentration of key sectors among a few large conglomerates was having "deleterious effects", adding that the wealth of India's five richest families had grown by 400 per cent while the real wages of salaried workers had fallen.Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said one quarter of 7.8 per cent growth did not amount to an "economic spring"."One quarter of 7.8 per cent growth is not an economic spring. If India has truly 'bloomed', why do rampant unemployment, leaked exam papers, and a crumbling education system define the ground reality?" he said."Why is the republic's prosperity not translating into the prosperity of its public?" Khera asked.Taking aim at the prime minister's remarks, he said GDP measures national output rather than jobs, wages or opportunities."Modi can manage his headlines. For India's youth, the question remains the same as ever: Where are the jobs?" Khera said.The Congress's criticism came after government data released on Monday showed that India's economy grew by a faster-than-expected 7.8 per cent in the April-June quarter.The growth figure exceeded the Reserve Bank of India's forecast of 7 per cent for the quarter and kept India as the world's fastest-growing major economy.Responding to the data, PM Modi took a dig at those questioning the state of the Indian economy, saying "doomsayers were doomed and India bloomed yet again".The prime minister said India's GDP growth during the first quarter of FY 2026-27 was a "herculean feat"."The collective strength of our people ensured India delivered such growth despite oil price shocks and supply chain issues in the midst of global uncertainties," PM Modi said in a post on X.The Q1 growth compares with a 6.9 per cent expansion in the year-ago quarter.The RBI has projected India's economy to grow by 6.7 per cent in the full 2026-27 fiscal year.

NEW DELHI: Punjab’s groundwater crisis is showing signs of improvement, with the latest assessment indicating a decline in groundwater extraction and an increase in canal-water utilisation, AAP Punjab media in-charge Baltej Pannu said on Monday.Addressing a press conference in Chandigarh earlier today, Pannu attributed the improvement to the Bhagwant Mann government’s efforts to strengthen canal infrastructure, increase the use of canal water and reduce dependence on groundwater.Pannu said canal-water utilisation has risen to around 80-82% from roughly 21% in 2022. He said the government had activated 14,100 watercourses, restored more than 400 km of defunct canals and concretised over 1,000 km of canals. Recharge points have also been developed along repaired canal infrastructure, he said.According to Pannu, Punjab’s stage of groundwater extraction declined from 163.80% in 2021-22 to 156.36% in 2025 and 152.22% in 2025-26. Annual groundwater extraction also fell from around 28.01 billion cubic metres to 26.32 billion cubic metres.Pannu said the latest assessment showed improvement in 95 of Punjab’s 153 dark-zone blocks, while the number of critical blocks fell from 10 to six.Four blocks — Arniwala in Fazilka, Makhu in Ferozepur, Hajipur in Hoshiarpur and Narot Jaimal Singh in Pathankot — have moved into the safe category, he said.Another 14 blocks have recorded significant improvement, according to Pannu.Pannu said total annual groundwater recharge has increased to 19.14 billion cubic metres, including 5.53 billion cubic metres from rainfall and 5.5 billion cubic metres through canal water. Canal-water recharge increased from 4.5 billion cubic metres last year to 5.5 billion cubic metres this year, he said.

Article Title: 'Vishwaguru, not a Mahashakti': RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat highlights India's legacy of refuge, global service in Toronto
Article Text:

TORONTO: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) Chief Mohan Bhagwat stated that India became a "Vishwaguru" (world teacher) through its selfless service to humanity rather than by acting as a "Mahashakti" (superpower), emphasising that the country's civilisational DNA is rooted in universal friendship, refuge, and respect for diversity.Addressing the "Hindu Vishwa Bandhu - Embrace the World in Friendship" gathering in Toronto, Bhagwat highlighted India's historical role as a sanctuary for those fleeing persecution and war worldwide."One may call Bharat a superpower, but it was not one. It served the world and by its own character, it became 'Vishwaguru', not Mahashakti," he said.Bhagwat recalled historical and modern examples of India stepping up during international humanitarian crises. Recalling the plight of Polish refugees during the Second World War, he noted how the Maharaja of Jamnagar offered them refuge and protection until they could safely return home."There are so many instances; it is still continuing," Bhagwat said, referring to Bharat's tradition of extending assistance during crises.Pointing to modern conflict evacuations in the Middle East, he highlighted how Indian military transport aircraft rescued not only Indian citizens but also nationals from seven other countries trapped in the war zone."When, some years back in the Middle East war, people were trapped, the military planes of Bharat went there and rescued not only Bharatiya citizens; citizens of seven countries were rescued from there by Bharatiya," he said.He noted that Muslims, Christians, Jews, and Parsis have historically found peaceful refuge and knowledge in India without fear of persecution."Anywhere in the world, if someone was persecuted, he got asylum in Bharat only," Bhagwat said.The RSS chief contrasted India's historic global outreach with imperial expansionism, stating that Indian civilisation spread knowledge rather than dominance."Our ancestors travelled from Mexico to Siberia... They crossed the Himalayas on foot, went to Southeast Asia through small boats, but they conquered no country. They gave knowledge, astronomy, ayurveda, imparted civilisational values... Even today, when an ordinary Bharatiya goes to any country, the people there offer Namaskara," he added.Underscoring Bharat's civilisational tradition of helping others, the RSS chief said the country never refused assistance when people in distress sought its help and often extended help without being asked."This is the tradition. This is the DNA of Bharat," he said.Defining the essence of Hindu philosophy, Bhagwat clarified that the identity transcends narrow linguistic or religious boundaries."When I say Hindu, the word Hindu cannot be defined by any specific language, through any specific worship, or through any living style," he said, adding that Hindus "respect all" and "accept all".Bhagwat also called for embracing diversity while recognising the underlying unity of humanity."We have to serve, accept, respect this diversity because it is an expression of unity. It beautifies it. It is the decoration. We celebrate it," he said.He said Bharat's ancient ethos recognises diversity as natural while regarding unity as the fundamental reality."There have been many castes, many creeds, many languages. Everything is many. Nothing"Nature, expression of reality, is diverse. Diversity is natural. Unity is the reality. You have to tackle with natural, keeping in mind reality. That is the ancient ethos of Bharat," he added.Emphasising the philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, Bhagwat said those who are open-minded and knowledgeable recognise the idea that the entire world is one family."Those who are open-minded and knowledgeable embrace the concept of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam--the belief that the entire earth is one family," he said.He said that while people may differ in their physical appearance, "in essence, we are all one", making service to others a duty."Therefore, serving others is our duty. We have gained this wisdom, which brings us enduring happiness and satisfaction," Bhagwat said. (ANI)
Article Summary: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) Chief Mohan Bhagwat said India became a "Vishwaguru" (world teacher) through its selfless service to humanity. He said the country's civilisational DNA is rooted in universal friendship, refuge, and respect for diversity.

Article Title: IISc sets up quantum computing hub under National Quantum Mission
Article Text:
The new Section 8 company will serve as the Quantum Computing Thematic Hub at IISc under the Union Govt’s National Quantum Mission

BENGALURU: IISc has set up a not-for-profit company to help build India’s capabilities in quantum computing, a technology expected to play a role in areas ranging from scientific research and industry to computing and communications in the coming years.Called the Foundation for QC Innovation (FQCI), the new Section 8 company will serve as the Quantum Computing Thematic Hub at IISc under the Union Govt’s National Quantum Mission.It’s one of four thematic hubs set up under the mission and will bring together researchers, academic institutions, industry and startups to develop quantum computing technologies in India.Quantum computers use the principles of quantum physics to process certain kinds of information differently from conventional computers. While the technology is still at an early stage, countries and companies around the world are investing heavily in it because of its potential to solve some problems that are difficult for existing computers.At IISc, the new hub will work across several approaches to building quantum computers, including systems based on light particles, superconducting circuits, semiconductor devices, neutral atoms and trapped ions.It will also work on quantum algorithms.“The National Quantum Mission provides a unique opportunity to build a strong and globally competitive quantum computing ecosystem in India. Our focus is on bringing together India’s research capabilities, advanced infrastructure, industry and entrepreneurial talent to translate cutting-edge research into indigenous quantum computing technologies and applications,” Shankar Kumar Selvaraja, project director, FQCI and professor, Centre for Nano Science and Engineering at IISc, said.A major part of the initiative will be the creation of shared facilities for making, testing and characterising quantum devices. The aim is to give researchers and companies access to infrastructure that can help move laboratory research towards working technologies.“FQCI will also focus on building the workforce and startup ecosystem required for the sector. Its programmes will support student research and internships, industry-academia collaboration, startup development and knowledge-sharing. The initiative has launched programmes called QC Rise, QC Bridge, QC Leap, QC Accel and QC Quest as part of these efforts,” IISc said.The larger goal, it added, was to reduce dependence on overseas technology by developing quantum computing capabilities within the country.
Article Summary: IISc has set up a not-for-profit company to help build India’s capabilities in quantum computing. The technology is expected to play a role in areas ranging from scientific research and industry to computing and communications in the coming years.Quantum computers use the principles of quantum physics to process certain kinds of information differently from conventional computers.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to intervene against Cockroach Janata Party's protest march on September 5, saying that maintenance of law and order was primarily the responsibility of the government and police.A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana said that there is no reason to presume that the proposed demonstration would insult in any untoward incident."We will at least, as of now, presume everybody will behave in a peaceful manner. Right now there is no compelling circumstance to assume that any untoward thing will happen," the CJI observed.The bench issued notice to the Centre and Delhi Police and posted the next hearing for September 10, along with other matters concerning the student protests.This comes after a plea was filed by retired Delhi Police officer Rajendra Singh, seeking directions to ensure that large-scale demonstrations and protest marches in sensitive areas of the national capital are held only after obtaining requisite police permissions.The counsel, appearing for Singh, urged the apex court to hear the matter on September 3, citing the proposed march and the upcoming BRICS Summit in Delhi on September 12-13.The counsel referred to the violence during the July 20 Sansad March announced by the CJP and cautioned that another incident could occur, even if not directly attributable to the organisers.The CJI, however, said the court could not proceed on the assumption that something untoward would happen and reiterated that the police authorities were competent to deal with any law-and-order situation."Before us, there is no identified group. You please impress upon the Union or NCT Delhi. It's for them to maintain law and order. They should act as per law," the CJI said."They are expected to maintain law and order, and the enforcing agency has the responsibility to maintain law and order... Article Title: Year-wise plan to implement Samudra Manthan in works
Article Text:
Petroleum minister Hardeep Puri reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval, said officials. (Photo: IANS)

NEW DELHI: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan, a Rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.Officials said petroleum minister Hardeep Puri recently reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions held in Gurgaon in Haryana and Duliajan in Assam, on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval last month.The year-wise roadmap will help government carry out exploration and production activities in a concerted manner across Krishna-Godavari (KG), Mahanadi, Andaman and Cauvery basins and ensure systematic utilisation of funds, an official said.The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks, and development of shared offshore production and evacuation infrastructure.While Rs 43,200 crore has been earmarked for drilling 60 exploratory deepwater wells over five years, Rs 28,534 crore has been allocated for acquisition of 2D and 3D seismic data, Rs 10,000 crore for common infrastructure hubs and Rs 2,000 crore for an oil and gas manufacturing and services zone.India’s annual crude oil requirement is around 256 million tonnes (MT), of which nearly 88 per cent is imported. Domestic crude oil production from 26 sedimentary basins is estimated at around 28 MT. With domestic output stagnating even as demand continues to rise, government has been looking to step up exploration to improve energy security and reduce import dependence.Samudra Manthan is expected to add more than 600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE) to the country’s hydrocarbon reserves and boost domestic production of crude oil and natural gas.Officials said government has implemented a series of upstream sector reforms over the past decade, including opening up almost the entire offshore acreage for exploration, changes to legal and contractual framework, and strengthening National Data Repository. Samudra Manthan would complement these reforms by providing public funding for offshore exploration and facilitating the deployment of advanced technologies, they said.The scheme also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country.
Article Summary: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan. The scheme is aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.

Article Title: India & China announce 8-point boundary consensus before Xi's visit, target early & substantial harvest in border delimitation
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question - co-chaired by Ajit Doval and Wang Yi this week - had led to an 8-point consensus, signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month.These included advancing consultations for an "early and substantial harvest" of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, expanding trans-border trade and rivers cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the SR talks.Building upon the outcomes from the last round of talks in 2024, the 2 sides agreed that the Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management would advance discussions on an “Early and Substantial Harvest” of boundary delimitation and Border Management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective Terms of Reference, said the joint statement.India and China had agreed last year to set up an expert group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC), to explore early harvest in boundary delimitation in the India-China border areas.The formulation was changed to early and substantial on this occasion.Two additional meeting points for military talks and 2 more channels of border military hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors were agreed upon to reinforce border management measures, according to both sides.“The two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR Talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution,” said the MEA in a statement. Unlike the Chinese readout of the talks on Tuesday, the joint statement did not mention package settlement or solution, although the 2005 agreement talks about making adjustments to reach a package settlement.The two sides also reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the guidance received from Modi and Xi, maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas and creating an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations.According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. “The two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management,” said the joint statement.Both sides also noted the progress on trans-border cooperation, with the Indian side appreciating the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Indian official pilgrimage Kailash-Manasarovar Yatra (KMY) in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.“Both sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with the view to work together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas,” said the joint statement.India and China also agreed to hold the next meeting of the India-China Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in September and maintain communication on issues including hydrological data sharing, and renewal of the relevant MoUs. It’s important for India that China shares hydrological information during emergency situations based on humanitarian considerations. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India in 2027.
Article Summary: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question had led to an 8-point consensus. The consensus signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India in 2027.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday urged Indians to embrace the ‘vocal for local’ mantra, asking people to avoid foreign holidays, hosting weddings abroad and buying gold unless necessary, while hailing the country's robust GDP growth. He linked the appeal to his broader push for Swadeshi and self-reliance, saying these efforts would help sustain India's growth and create opportunities for its youth.In a video message posted on social media, PM Modi congratulated the people of India on the country's 7.8% GDP growth in the April-June quarter, saying the achievement was possible because of their “collective resolve and efforts”.He highlighted the fact that India had achieved the growth milestone despite conflicts, wars, global instability and supply-chain disruptions. He noted that there had been little stability globally since the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, but India had continued to make progress.“We have to maintain the speed of our growth. We have to grow. And for that we must become self-reliant,” PM Modi said, adding that the dreams of India's youth would require sustained effort.He said continued focus on Swadeshi and self-reliance could help present the country's youth with a developed India when the nation marks 100 years of Independence.The Prime Minister also said his government's policies and intentions were clear and credited them for helping India reach “new heights of progress”. He alleged that attempts were being made to spread negativity and falsehood in the country, but said India had continued to grow despite them.India's economy grew 7.8% year-on-year in the April-June quarter of 2026-27, beating expectations and showing resilience despite concerns over the economic impact of the West Asia conflict. Growth, however, moderated from 8.6% in the previous quarter.
Article Summary: PM Modi hails India's 7.8% GDP growth, says youth dreams need sustained effort. He urges Indians to embrace the ‘vocal for local’ mantra, asking people to avoid foreign holidays, hosting weddings abroad and buying gold unless necessary.

SAHARANPUR: Real currency notes worth Rs 7.4 crore were replaced with fake ones at a Punjab National Bank (PNB) money vault in Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh Police have registered an FIR against bank officials and private individuals, and a Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been formed to probe the improbable heist.The case was registered at Sadar police station based on a complaint filed by PNB nodal officer Arun Kumar Chaubey. The FIR names senior divisional manager Ravi Kumar, currency chest managers Sushil Sharma and Amit Kumar as primary suspects.In a parallel development, a separate report was filed against a housekeeper, Vishal Kumar, regarding a “distinct cash shortfall” at the bank.According to PNB chief deputy manager Nisha Singh, the fraud began unravelling when a cash remittance dispatched to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Aug 10 revealed a shortage of ₹4.36 lakh. A detailed audit ordered by RBI uncovered the startling influx of counterfeit notes.“An inquiry is in progress, and once we have complete details and evidence against everyone involved, the findings will be made public. The final tally of fake currency is still being verified as counting continues,” said Singh.Saharanpur DIG Abhishek said, “An SIT has been constituted and an FIR filed against those allegedly involved. Counting is in progress. Following a detailed inquiry, the embezzled currency will be recovered,” he said.Investigators are currently scrutinising bank transaction records, audit ledgers and CCTV footage from the currency chest to trace how the counterfeit bills were smuggled in and pinpoint all individuals involved in the operation.
Article Summary: Real currency notes worth Rs 7.4 crore were replaced with fake ones at a Punjab National Bank (PNB) money vault in Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh. Police have registered an FIR against bank officials and private individuals. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been formed to probe the improbable heist.

Article Title: Rupee gains 26 paise as 7.8% GDP growth offsets global market jitters
Article Text:
Rupee jumps 26 paise against US dollar

Rupee began Tuesday on a strong note, rising 26 paise to 94.96 against the US dollar in early trade, supported by robust domestic economic growth, containing fiscal slippage and portfolio-related inflows.Forex traders said the USD/INR pair appears to have found a strong near-term base around 95.10-95.20. MSCI-related inflows have also provided temporary support to the rupee.At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 95.06 against the US dollar before gaining further to touch 94.96. The currency had closed 21 paise higher at 95.22 on Monday after recovering from its initial losses.The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 99.46, up 0.03 per cent.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, rose 0.63 per cent to $91.06 a barrel in futures trade. The increase came after US President Donald Trump warned that the United States would "hit Iran hard" following missile attacks on American military bases in Jordan.Rupee's gains came even as domestic equities started Tuesday's session on a weaker note. The Sensex declined 121.48 points to 76,835.79 in early trade, while the Nifty fell 52.6 points to 24,027.80.Foreign institutional investors remained sellers in the equity market, offloading shares worth Rs 7,985.88 crore on a net basis on Monday, according to exchange data.Despite the recent selling, FPIs invested around USD 3.1 billion in August. This was their strongest monthly inflow in 23 months and marked the second consecutive month of net buying.However, foreign investors have remained net sellers of around USD 24.6 billion so far in 2026."So, the direction has improved -- but the broader foreign-flow picture is still not completely comfortable," Pabari added.India's economic growth also provided support to the rupee. The economy expanded 7.8 per cent in the April-June quarter, beating expectations and showing resilience despite concerns that the war in Iran and the resulting global economic uncertainty could weigh on growth."The data is particularly noteworthy because it came during a period marked by Middle East tensions and elevated crude prices. Strong growth does not automatically strengthen a currency, but it does reinforce the perception that India's domestic economy remains resilient despite global turbulence," CR Forex Advisors MD Amit Pabari said.The fiscal position also remained a factor in the currency market. The central government's fiscal deficit for 2026-27 stood at 26.8 per cent of the full-year target at the end of July, according to data released by the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) on Monday.In comparison, the fiscal deficit had stood at 29.9 per cent of the Budget Estimates (BE) of 2025-26 during the first four months of the previous financial year.
Article Summary: Rupee rises 26 paise to 94.96 against the US dollar in early trade. Rupee's gains came even as domestic equities started Tuesday's session on a weaker note. Sensex declined 121.48 points to 76,835.79, while Nifty fell 52.6 points to 24,027.80.

Article Title: First-time voters can apply to be on SIR list by September 30 in Maharashtra
Article Text:
2cr(approx) fewer electors than the earlier voter list in Maharashtra’s SIR draft electoral roll (AI Image)





MUMBAI: The draft voter li­st of Maharashtra’s special int­e­nsive revision, pu­b­lished on Monday, has 2 cr­o­re fewer voters than the previous electoral roll. Mumbai is down by 36 lakh voters — a 35% fall.The electoral roll used ti­ll June had 9.8 crore voters, while the draft SIR roll has 7.7 crore voters, which is 21.1% lower. However, in real terms there are 1.9 crore fewer voters in the state on the draft list since 17 lakh voters were removed from one constituency owing to duplicati­on, but ha­ve been retained in the other. “The 17 lakh duplicate voters cannot be considered as excluded,” state chi­ef electoral officer S Chockalingam said.The reduction in voters is because their enumerati­on forms were not collected owing to them being reported as absent, shifted their residen­ce, dead or duplicate.Around 1.5cr of the 2cr vo­ters whose names have be­en excluded will have the opportunity to apply to be on the SIR list until Sept 30.This is the phase of filing claims and objections to the draft roll. First-time voters who turned 18 before Oct 1 can also apply to be on the SIR voter list during this one-month period till Sept.“Around 34 lakh voters were reported dead, while 17 lakh were related to duplicate registrations. Hence, around 1.5 crore of the 2 crore voters whose names have been excluded because they were absent or had shifted residence have the opportunity to apply to be on the electoral roll,” said Chockalingam.Citizens can check their names on the draft roll on the ECI portal https://voters.eci.gov.in and website of the state’s chief electoral officer https://ceoelection.maharashtra.gov.in/ceo/ as well as the website of the district election officers. The draft rolls are also available with recognised political parties at the district level.If citizens have been excluded from the list after they filled out the enumeration form and even if they have missed filling the enumeration form, they can fill out Form 6 to be included on the SIR voter list. They can also fill out Form 7 for deletion from the list and Form 8 for corrections in name, address, gender and so on.These forms can be filled out online on the above sites. Also, citizens can approach electoral registration officers in their assembly constituency — their addresses are on the website of the state’s chief electoral officer. Citizens can also approach booth level officers or block level agents appointed by political parties.Of the total 7.7 crore voters in the SIR draft list in the state, 3.9 crore are male and 3.7 crore female. Of the 2 crore voters who have not been included in the draft roll owing to uncollected forms, the highest numbers are from urban areas as a result of internal shifting and migration. While Mumbai had the highest number, the other key cities with exclusions were Pune (28.6 lakh), Thane (28.5 lakh) and Nagpur (14.4 lakh).
Article Summary: The electoral roll used ti­ll June had 9.8 crore voters, while the draft SIR roll has 7.7 crore voters. The reduction in voters is because their enumerati­on forms were not collected owing to them being reported as absent, shifted their residen­ce, dead or duplicate. Of the 2 crore voters who have not been included in the draft roll owing to uncollected forms, the highest numbers are from urban areas.

Article Summary: IMD warns of very heavy rainfall in Chhattisgarh, east Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Uttarakhand. Odisha may also see thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds.
